source: Michie et al. (2013), Behavior Change Technique Taxonomy v1
catalogue_scope: Researcher-selected 38-technique Sensei runtime subset of the 93-item BCTTv1, suitable for consideration by a non-clinical health and wellbeing coaching Advisor. It is not the full taxonomy, not a scenario mapping, and selection is never mandatory.
redistribution_note: Identifiers and labels follow BCTTv1. Definitions are concise runtime paraphrases; source examples and coding notes are omitted. Verify source terms before redistributing quoted taxonomy text.

entries.name: Goal setting (behavior)
entries.definition: Set or mutually agree a goal expressed as the behavior the person intends to perform.

entries.name: Problem solving
entries.definition: Analyse influences on the behavior with the person and identify strategies for barriers or facilitators.

entries.name: Goal setting (outcome)
entries.definition: Set or mutually agree a goal expressed as a desired outcome of behavior.

entries.name: Action planning
entries.definition: Develop a plan that specifies when, where, how, or how often the behavior will be performed.

entries.name: Review behavior goal(s)
entries.definition: Review progress toward behavior goals and consider keeping, revising, or replacing them collaboratively.

entries.name: Discrepancy between current behavior and goal
entries.definition: Draw attention to a grounded difference between current behavior and a previously chosen goal.

entries.name: Review outcome goal(s)
entries.definition: Review progress toward outcome goals and consider keeping, revising, or replacing them collaboratively.

entries.name: Commitment
entries.definition: Invite the person to affirm or strengthen a voluntary commitment to the behavior.

entries.name: Feedback on behavior
entries.definition: Provide feedback based on measured or otherwise observed performance of the behavior.

entries.name: Self-monitoring of behavior
entries.definition: Establish a method for the person to record or observe their own behavior.

entries.name: Self-monitoring of outcome(s) of behavior
entries.definition: Establish a method for the person to record or observe outcomes associated with their behavior.

entries.name: Biofeedback
entries.definition: Provide feedback about a bodily process using an external measurement method.

entries.name: Feedback on outcome(s) of behavior
entries.definition: Provide feedback based on measured or otherwise observed outcomes of behavior.

entries.name: Social support (unspecified)
entries.definition: Advise, arrange, or encourage social support without specifying practical or emotional form.

entries.name: Social support (practical)
entries.definition: Advise, arrange, or encourage practical help from other people for the behavior.

entries.name: Social support (emotional)
entries.definition: Advise, arrange, or encourage emotional support from other people for the behavior.

entries.name: Instruction on how to perform the behavior
entries.definition: Explain or agree on how the behavior can be performed, within the Advisor's scope.

entries.name: Information about antecedents
entries.definition: Provide information about situations or events that reliably precede the behavior.

entries.name: Behavioral experiments
entries.definition: Agree on a safe behavioral test that lets the person examine a belief or prediction through experience.

entries.name: Information about health consequences
entries.definition: Provide relevant general information about health consequences without making a personal clinical claim.

entries.name: Information about social and environmental consequences
entries.definition: Provide information about social or environmental consequences of performing the behavior.

entries.name: Demonstration of the behavior
entries.definition: Show or describe a clear model of how the behavior can be performed.

entries.name: Prompts/cues
entries.definition: Introduce or identify a prompt that can remind the person to perform the behavior.

entries.name: Behavioral practice/rehearsal
entries.definition: Prompt practice or rehearsal so performance of the behavior can develop.

entries.name: Behavior substitution
entries.definition: Replace an unwanted behavior with a chosen alternative behavior.

entries.name: Habit formation
entries.definition: Encourage repeated performance in a consistent context so the behavior becomes habitual.

entries.name: Graded tasks
entries.definition: Begin with an achievable version of the behavior and increase difficulty in manageable stages.

entries.name: Credible source
entries.definition: Present relevant information as coming from a source the person can reasonably regard as credible.

entries.name: Pros and cons
entries.definition: Help the person consider personally relevant advantages and disadvantages of changing or not changing.

entries.name: Reduce negative emotions
entries.definition: Identify a non-clinical strategy intended to reduce difficult emotions that interfere with the behavior.

entries.name: Restructuring the physical environment
entries.definition: Change objects or features of the physical environment to support the behavior.

entries.name: Restructuring the social environment
entries.definition: Change the social setting or social arrangements to support the behavior.

entries.name: Avoidance/reducing exposure to cues for the behavior
entries.definition: Reduce exposure to environmental or social cues that prompt an unwanted behavior.

entries.name: Adding objects to the environment
entries.definition: Add an object to the person's environment to make the chosen behavior easier or more likely.

entries.name: Framing/reframing
entries.definition: Offer a different perspective on the behavior that may alter how it is understood or approached.

entries.name: Verbal persuasion about capability
entries.definition: Express a grounded message intended to strengthen belief in the person's ability to perform the behavior.

entries.name: Focus on past success
entries.definition: Invite attention to relevant behaviors or goals the person has previously accomplished.

entries.name: Self-talk
entries.definition: Prompt the person to use a chosen self-statement that can support performance of the behavior.
